summary: Craven County, NC, steel fire tower built by the CCC in 1935; NHLR-registered 2021; may have been sold at a 2018 state auction, so current owner and condition are unclear.

facts.design: Steel tower 99 ft 9 in tall with a five-room ground house, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
facts.status_note: NHLR: appeared to be in good condition as of 2020 and may have been sold at a 2018 state auction. No later source confirms the current owner or condition.

corrections.why: The 1935 build record gives 99 feet 9 inches, which is about 30.4 m. The 30.2 m figure looks like 99 feet rounded down. The Register's 50-75 foot figure is an estimate, not a measurement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 build record gives 99 feet 9 inches (about 30.4 m). The NHLR page gives an estimate of 50 to 75 feet and says it appears to be that tall. The story uses the 1935 figure for the build height and reports the estimate as a disagreement.

The NHLR says the tower appeared to be in good condition in 2020 and may have been sold at a 2018 state auction. No readable source confirms the owner or the condition since then, so the record keeps standing with a status note.

notes_for_editor: Staffing and notable fires are not in any readable source. A 2002 Wilmington Star-News obituary (seen only as a search snippet; fetch returned HTTP 403) says Willow Atkinson Baker began as Wilmar Fire Tower operator in about 1958. Not used because it could not be read. 2024 social posts call the tower abandoned; not used as sources. Confirm the 2018 auction and current owner with the NC Forest Service or the county before publishing. The NHLR page is the only source for the post-1936 history.
